From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@edenbank.com>

Date: Sun, 3 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant PEK escrow and rotation clarification

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the quick response during onboarding last week. The Eden security team is compiling our SIG/CAIQ evidence package and we have a few follow-ups specific to tenant-level encryption and key custody before the SOC 2 review next month. Can you help confirm the following?

1) Do you use a per-tenant PEK (payload-encryption key) that is wrapped by a tenant KEK in an HSM, or is the PEK a derived value stored only in Redis/KV? We need a short narrative explaining where PEKs originate and how they are protected at rest.

2) Escrow: Do you retain any form of tenant key escrow for recovery? If so, what is the escrow process, who can request a recover (teams & roles), and where is the escrow material stored?

3) Rotation cadence and canary process: What is the documented rotation cadence for tenant KEKs and PEKs? If you rotate tenant KEKs, do you perform a staged/canary rotation and can you provide a sample rotation run (redacted) showing the steps, timestamps, and verification checks?

4) HSM attestation and operator access: Please share the latest HSM attestation (FIPS/attestation report) and an export of the operator ACL snapshot for the KMS cluster (we will redact IDs as needed).

If you can provide a short one-page summary addressing 1-4 plus sample artifacts (redacted rotation logs, attestation PDF, ACL snapshot), that would be ideal. We can accept redacted CSVs and a single zipped package.

Target for our auditor intake is COB next Wednesday — is that feasible?

Thank you,
Laura Chen
Information Security — Eden Bank
security@edenbank.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 3 Aug 2025 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant PEK escrow and rotation clarification

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list. Summarized answers below and weve started gathering the artifacts. Full artifacts will be uploaded to the secure share linked at the bottom.

Quick answers:
- PEK handling: We generate a per-tenant ephemeral PEK on first write. PEKs are encrypted (wrapped) by a tenant KEK which is stored in the KMS backed by an HSM. The PEK itself is not stored in plaintext in our data stores; only the wrapped PEK blob is persisted alongside metadata.
- Escrow: We do not keep a separate offsite escrow containing unwrapped PEKs. Recovery is supported via the KEK recovery process: KEKs are recoverable by the HSM SNK escrow mechanism when authorized by an account-level emergency recovery runbook and a two-person ops approval (see artifacts).
- Rotation: Tenant KEKs are rotated on a quarterly cadence by default; PEKs are rewrapped during KEK rotation for active tenants. We run a staged canary rotation on a small percentage of tenants, verify token-level decryption and end-to-end checks, then proceed to full rollout.
- HSM attestation & operator ACLs: Attestation PDF and operator ACL snapshot are included in the package; operator access is restricted to the KMS team and requires LDAP + MFA and justification in our privileged access system.

Next steps / deliverables:
1) We will upload: redwood_hsm_attestation_2024.pdf, pek_rotation_sample_log_2025-07-18.csv (redacted), operator_acl_snapshot_2025-07-31.csv (redacted), kms_config_snapshot_2025-07.json.
2) I will add a concise one-page narrative for your SIG/CAIQ intake covering the four points.
3) Marissa will confirm timeline for redaction and checksums.

We expect to have the package to you by EOD Monday (2025-08-04) and will push to the secure drive: https://redwood.app/drive/edenbank/kms-evidence-2025

If you need stricter redaction or a different file format for auditors, let us know.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
